report.summary: The cause was in `public/src/retry.js`. `withRetry` stopped retrying when a read failed with HTTP 503 on any attempt after the first, so a 503 outage got one retry instead of three. The panel then showed "Service health unavailable" after about 1s and waited for Retry. I removed that early exit. A failed read is now retried after 1, 2 and 4 seconds, and the panel shows the services as soon as a retry succeeds. After the last failure it still shows "Service health unavailable" with Retry, as HLT-2 requires. The only file changed is `public/src/retry.js`. `health.js` is the only caller of `withRetry`.
report.verification: `npm test` passes (4/4), but those tests don't cover the 503 case. I ran the Recovery Probe check `checks/health.json` (two HTTP 503 failures on page load, no Retry click) on the original code and on the fixed code. Original: fail, RECOVERY_NOT_OBSERVED, and the screen stayed on "Service health unavailable Retry". Fixed: pass, RECOVERED, with the services shown about 3.3s after load (the 1s and 2s retries) and no Retry click. I did not use `compare_reports` or `verify_change`. The project has no `.recovery-probe/verify.json`, and my baseline came from stashing the change in the same working tree, not from a separate checkout of main. The check covers only two 503 failures on page load. It does not cover the message after the third retry fails, or other kinds of failure. I started the server myself for the check and stopped it by its process id.
